name: Heavy
desc: Small creatures have disadvantage on attack rolls with heavy weapons. A heavy weapon's size and bulk make it too large for a Small creature to use effectively.
content: The Heavy property imposes disadvantage on attack rolls for small creatures using heavy weapons due to the size and bulk of these weapons. Small creatures are not able to effectively wield heavy weapons, impacting their combat effectiveness. This property is linked to the "Heavy" weapon index and can be found at the specified URL.

name: Ammunition
desc: You can use a weapon that has the ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from the weapon. Each time you attack with the weapon, you expend one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition from a quiver, case, or other container is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon).

At the end of the battle, you can recover half your expended ammunition by taking a minute to search the battlefield. If you use a weapon that has the ammunition property to make a melee attack, you treat the weapon as an improvised weapon (see "Improvised Weapons" later in the section). A sling must be loaded to deal any damage when used in this way.
content: The Ammunition property allows you to make ranged attacks with a weapon only if you have ammunition available, with each attack expending one piece of ammunition. You can recover half of your expended ammunition after battle by searching the battlefield. If using a weapon with the ammunition property for a melee attack, it is treated as an improvised weapon. Note that a sling must be loaded to deal damage in this manner. Having a free hand is necessary to load a one-handed weapon with ammunition.

name: Finesse
desc: When making an attack with a finesse weapon, you use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.
content: The Finesse property allows the wielder of a finesse weapon to choose between using their Strength or Dexterity modifier for both attack and damage rolls, emphasizing agility and precision in combat. This property is particularly useful for characters who excel in dexterity-based skills and abilities, providing flexibility in their choice of attribute for combat effectiveness.

name: Loading
desc: Because of the time required to load this weapon, you can fire only one piece of ammunition from it when you use an action, bonus action, or reaction to fire it, regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.
content: The Loading property restricts firing only one piece of ammunition from a weapon per action, bonus action, or reaction, regardless of the usual number of attacks allowed. This limitation is due to the time required to load the weapon, emphasizing the importance of strategic ammunition management in combat situations.

name: Light
desc: A light weapon is small and easy to handle, making it ideal for use when fighting with two weapons.
content: The Light (light) weapon is small and easy to handle, perfect for dual-wielding in combat scenarios. It is described as ideal for quick, agile movements and precise strikes. This weapon property enhances the wielder's dexterity and coordination skills, allowing for swift and efficient attacks.

name: Reach
desc: This weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, as well as when determining your reach for opportunity attacks with it.
content: The Reach weapon property extends your attack range by 5 feet, affecting both your regular attacks and opportunity attacks. This property is named Reach and can be found under the index 'reach'. It enhances your reach without the need for additional movement, providing a strategic advantage in combat situations.

name: Special
desc: A weapon with the special property has unusual rules governing its use, explained in the weapon's description (see "Special Weapons" later in this section).
content: The Special weapon property denotes a weapon with unique rules that govern its usage, as detailed in the description provided. This property is explained further in the section dedicated to Special Weapons.

name: Monk
desc: Monks gain several benefits while unarmed or wielding only monk weapons while they aren't wearing armor or wielding shields.
content: Monk: Monks gain benefits when unarmed or wielding monk weapons without armor or shields.

name: Versatile
desc: This weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property--the damage when the weapon is used with two hands to make a melee attack.
content: The Versatile property allows a weapon to be used with one or two hands, providing a damage value in parentheses for two-handed melee attacks. This property enhances the weapon's flexibility in combat, requiring both strength and dexterity to wield effectively.

name: Two-Handed
desc: This weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.
content: The Two-Handed weapon property requires the use of both hands when attacking. This property is commonly associated with weapons that are larger or heavier, requiring increased strength and coordination from the wielder. It is essential for players to consider the Two-Handed property when selecting weapons for combat scenarios, as it can impact their strategy and effectiveness in battle.

name: Thrown
desc: If a weapon has the thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack. If the weapon is a melee weapon, you use the same ability modifier for that attack roll and damage roll that you would use for a melee attack with the weapon. For example, if you throw a handaxe, you use your Strength, but if you throw a dagger, you can use either your Strength or your Dexterity, since the dagger has the finesse property.
content: The Thrown property allows a weapon to be thrown for ranged attacks, using the same ability modifier as for melee attacks with the weapon. For example, a handaxe uses Strength, while a dagger can use either Strength or Dexterity due to the finesse property.
